state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s presented to the emergency department with 5 days of nausea and vomiting. He noted chronic, left-sided abdominal pain and normal passage of stool and flatus. Past medical history was unremarkable. Current medications included only esomeprazole.

Vital signs: Afebrile, normotensive, pulse rate 104/minute. Abdominal exam revealed a large, firm, tender mass located near the umbilicus, without rigidity or rebound tenderness.

- Laboratory studies:    - Lactate: 6.3 mmol/L (reference range 0.7-2.2 mmol/L)    - Serial lactate measurements between 4.7-7.2 mmol/L    - Low bicarbonate, low PCO2, marginally acidotic pH on venous blood gas    - Urinalysis and blood cultures showed no evidence of infection      - Imaging studies:    CT Abdomen findings: Diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass abutting multiple segments of small intestine and encasing the mesenteric vasculature

root.label: Subacute Abdominal Pain Syndrome with Elevated Lactate and Mesenteric Mass
supporting_facts: large, firm, tender mass near the umbilicus
low bicarbonate, low PCO2, marginally acidotic pH on venous blood gas
